about: Single source for Mapflow AI models and scenarios. Read by the docs (source/_ext/mapflow_catalog.py), published with every docs build at /models.json for the website, Mapflow Web and the QGIS plugin. Prices must match awesome-configs/configs/default.

imagery_prices._note: Credits per km² for basemaps, by zoom. Mirrors userguides/_static/csv/data_prices.csv.

models.name: Buildings
models.image_alt: Building roof polygons over a suburban area
models.caption: Example result: one polygon per building roof.
models.summary: Roof outline of every building in your area, as editable polygons.
models.description: Finds building roofs on high-resolution imagery and returns one polygon per building. Objects under 20 m² are dropped to keep the layer clean. Building types, heights and cleaner shapes are options you switch on when you start a run.
models.output: A polygon layer of building roofs.
models.best_with: Aerial or satellite imagery at 0.6–0.3 m per pixel (zoom 18).
uses: Refresh a municipal building layer before a field survey
Count structures in a settlement for planning or emergency response
Find parcels with new or missing buildings

models.name: Forest and trees
models.image_alt: Tree and shrub cover mask over a residential area
models.caption: Example result: tree and shrub cover mask.
models.summary: All tree and shrub cover, down to small groups and tree lines.
models.description: Segments every area covered by trees and shrubs, including sparse forest and shrubland. It works in most environments, cities included. Height classes and individual tree crowns are options you switch on when you start a run.
models.output: A polygon layer of tree and shrub cover.
models.best_with: 0.6–0.15 m imagery (zoom 18–20) taken in the growing season. Leafless or snow-covered trees are not detected.
uses: Measure canopy cover per district or parcel
Compare two dates to find cleared forest
Build a green-space inventory for a city

models.name: Roads
models.image_alt: Road network polygons over a suburban area
models.caption: Example result: road polygons built from a cleaned centreline network.
models.summary: A connected road network with gaps merged and short stubs removed.
models.description: Finds road centrelines, cleans the graph (simplifies geometry, merges gaps, removes double edges and short detached pieces) and turns it back into road polygons. Multi-task learning keeps the network connected where trees or buildings hide the road.
models.output: Road polygons built from a cleaned centreline network.
models.best_with: Rural and suburban areas with 0.6–0.3 m imagery (zoom 18). Dense city centres with wide sidewalks and complex crossings are harder.

specs.geo_domain: Global, best in rural and suburban areas

uses: Map access roads and tracks for rural planning
Add forestry and field tracks missing from OSM
Check the street network in new suburbs

models.name: Buildings + Roads + Forest
models.image_alt: Buildings, roads and forest layers over a dense urban area
models.caption: Example result: buildings, roads and forest from one run.
models.summary: Buildings, roads and forest together, with topology corrected.
models.description: Runs the Buildings, Roads and Forest models as one workflow and returns a single topology-corrected result, so the layers do not overlap. It costs less than running the three models one by one.
models.output: Buildings, roads and forest from one run, as separate styled layers.

specs.method: Buildings, Roads and Forest + topology correction

uses: Start a base map where no vector data exists
Get a land-use overview before a site visit
Create a reference layer for disaster response

models.name: Open data
models.image_alt: OpenStreetMap buildings and roads over imagery
models.caption: Example result: OpenStreetMap and Overture layers for the area.
models.summary: OpenStreetMap and Overture data for your area, with no AI model involved.
models.description: Downloads the classes you choose from OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps for your area, so you can check coverage before running AI, or fill gaps after.
models.output: Vector layers for each class you select.
models.best_with: Any area. Quality depends on how complete open data is there, and it may not line up exactly with the imagery.

specs.method: No AI model: OpenStreetMap + Overture Maps

price.label: Shown before you run
price.note: No AI model is used. You still pick imagery as a visual reference.

uses: Check OSM completeness before paying for AI mapping
Combine open data with AI results
Add context layers to a project in one step

models.name: Constructions
models.image_alt: Construction site outlines in a fast-developing area
models.caption: Example result: construction sites in a fast-developing area.
models.summary: Outlines of construction sites and buildings under construction.
models.description: Outlines areas that contain construction sites and buildings under construction. Available for selected countries; coverage is growing.
models.best_with: 0.6–0.3 m satellite imagery (zoom 18) of fast-developing areas.
uses: Track new development for permits and taxes
Monitor progress on large projects
Flag unplanned construction

models.name: High-density housing
models.image_alt: Dense housing blocks split into individual houses
models.caption: Example result: dense blocks split into houses (Tunisia).
models.summary: Terraced and tightly packed blocks divided into individual houses.
models.description: Segments dense building blocks as a whole, then divides each block into individual houses from roof markers, using a grid or Voronoi split. Built for terraced and densely built areas common in the Middle East and parts of Africa.
models.output: Individual house polygons within dense blocks.
models.best_with: High-resolution imagery of terraced or densely built areas.

requirements.note: No configuration in default or customer; limits are set when the model is connected.

uses: Count dwellings in dense urban areas
Support census and address mapping
Plan services in informal settlements

models.name: Buildings (Aerial)
models.image_alt: Detailed building outlines on 10 cm aerial imagery
models.caption: Example result: rural residential area at 10 cm.
models.summary: Small buildings and detailed outlines from 15–10 cm aerial imagery.
models.description: Built for very high-resolution aerial imagery (15–10 cm per pixel) to extract small buildings and detailed outlines. Best in rural and suburban residential areas; for dense cities use the Buildings model, even on aerial imagery.
models.best_with: Aerial imagery at 10–5 cm (zoom 20–21) of low-rise areas.
uses: Map sheds and outbuildings on a drone survey
Capture detailed outlines for cadastre updates
Map rural settlements from a municipal flight

models.name: Solar panels
models.caption: Example result: rooftop and ground-mounted panels.
models.summary: Photovoltaic panels on rooftops and on the ground.
models.description: A detection and segmentation model for photovoltaic panels, trained on aerial imagery. It finds panels on rooftops and in solar farms.

requirements.note: No configuration in default or customer; values from the model page.

uses: Inventory rooftop solar in a municipality
Monitor solar farm build-out
Estimate installed panel area for grid planning

models.name: Swimming pools
models.image_alt: Detected swimming pools in a residential area
models.caption: Example result: pools detected and classified.
models.summary: Swimming pools detected and classified from aerial imagery.
models.description: Detects and classifies swimming pools on high-resolution aerial imagery, with a test score above F1 0.95.
models.output: Swimming pool polygons with a class.

requirements.note: No configuration in default or customer; values from the model page.

uses: Keep property records and tax rolls up to date
Plan water use and inspections
Enrich insurance and real-estate data

models.name: Agriculture fields
models.caption: Example result: field boundaries in Belgium.
models.summary: Field boundaries separated by tree lines, roads or crop stage.
models.description: Detects agricultural fields and separates neighbouring fields where a visible boundary exists. Tuned for larger fields in Europe with active vegetation; small and terraced fields are harder.
models.best_with: 1–1.2 m imagery in the growing season.

requirements.note: No configuration in default or customer; values from the model page.

uses: Build field boundaries for farm management
Estimate cultivated area per region
Prepare parcels for crop monitoring

models.name: Segment Anything
models.caption: Example result: SAM at zoom 16.
models.summary: Universal segmentation. The zoom level decides what you get.
models.description: Meta's universal segmentation model, adapted to Mapflow workflows. Zoom 14 outlines land use, large fields and water; zoom 16 small fields and large buildings; zoom 18 farms and groups of trees; zoom 19 and up houses, trees and vehicles.
models.output: Polygons of whatever stands out at the chosen zoom.
models.best_with: Any RGB imagery. Choose the zoom in the run form.

requirements.note: No configuration in default or customer; zoom is chosen in the run form.

uses: Outline objects no standard model covers
Pre-segment imagery for manual labelling
Explore a new area before choosing a model

scenarios.title: Map every building
scenarios.summary: Roof outline of every building in your area, as editable polygons.

scenarios.title: Sort buildings by type
scenarios.image_alt: Building polygons coloured by building type
scenarios.summary: Every building polygon carries a type, ready to filter and style.
scenarios.description: Runs the Buildings model with classification switched on, so each roof polygon gets a building class. Classification adds no extra cost.
scenarios.output: Building polygons with a class attribute.
scenarios.best_with: Aerial or satellite imagery at 0.6–0.3 m per pixel (zoom 18).
uses: Compare residential and non-residential stock by district
Pull industrial and commercial sites into their own layer
Feed zoning and land-use analysis with fresh data

scenarios.title: Building heights and 3D footprints
scenarios.image_alt: Building footprints extruded by estimated height
scenarios.summary: A height for each building, with the outline moved from roof to ground.
scenarios.description: Adds a height model that reads shadow length and visible walls. The result is a 3D footprint: the building contour projected to ground level instead of the roof outline.
scenarios.output: Footprint polygons with a height attribute, ready for the QGIS 3D map view.
scenarios.best_with: 0.6–0.3 m imagery (zoom 18) with visible shadows. Helps most on oblique imagery, where roofs look shifted.
uses: Extrude buildings in the QGIS 3D map view
Estimate floor area and building volume
Screen areas for shade and line-of-sight studies

scenarios.title: Map forest and tree cover
scenarios.summary: All tree and shrub cover, down to small groups and tree lines.

scenarios.title: Vegetation height along power lines
scenarios.image_alt: Vegetation height classes inside a power line corridor
scenarios.summary: Vegetation split into shrubs, 4–10 m forest and forest over 10 m.
scenarios.description: Runs the forest model with height estimation. Vegetation is classed as shrubs under 4 m, forest from 4 to 10 m and forest over 10 m, which is what vegetation managers need near power lines.
scenarios.output: Vegetation polygons with a height class.
scenarios.best_with: 0.6–0.3 m imagery (zoom 18–19) taken in the growing season.

requirements.note: From the workflow description; the workflow requirements apply.

uses: Prioritise clearance work in power line corridors
Plan right-of-way maintenance by height class
Screen vegetation along roads and railways
scenarios.tip: Buffer your line layer in QGIS (Vector › Geoprocessing › Buffer) and use the buffer as the area, so you pay only for the corridor.

scenarios.title: Count individual trees
scenarios.image_alt: A point for every tree crown on a golf course
scenarios.summary: A point for every tree crown, free-standing trees included.
scenarios.description: Extracts tree crowns from forest and from single trees, as points with a crown radius or as crown polygons.
scenarios.output: Tree crown points with a radius, or crown polygons.
scenarios.best_with: 0.3 m imagery (zoom 19) to separate individual trees.

requirements.note: From the CrownsPolygons/CrownsPoints block description; the workflow requirements apply.

uses: Street-tree and park inventories
Count trees in orchards and plantations
Track tree loss on a construction site

scenarios.title: Extract the road network
scenarios.summary: A connected road network with gaps merged and short stubs removed.

scenarios.title: Base map in one run
scenarios.summary: Buildings, roads and forest together, with topology corrected.
